name: H. A. C. Taylor House

dates.altered: Demolished 1952 for the subdivision of its grounds; some salvage went into the outbuildings of the adjacent Ocean Lawn (Wikimapia entry, a low-authority source recorded because no other fetched page states the demolition).
dates.note: The RISD Archives print is inscribed 'DATE: 1886'; the University at Buffalo record (from Scully) gives '1885 - 86'; the node's exemplar year is 1885.

refs.title: "H.A.C. Taylor House" by RISD McKim, Mead and White and RISD Archives (1939 Rhode Island Architecture Exhibition, archives identifier 23.4.4)
refs.note: Inscription on the verso, as the record prints it: 'H.A.C. TAYLOR HOUSE, Annandale Road, Newport. 1886. By McKim / Mead and White. The first Colonial Revival house; with academic plan, / eclectic eighteenth century detail and even the typical early Newport / gable-above-hip roof. (Rhode Island Architecture, Hitchcock.)'

refs.title: Henry-Russell Hitchcock, Rhode Island Architecture (1939), as quoted on the RISD print's inscription
refs.note: The book itself was not opened; the quotation reaches this record at one remove.

refs.note: 'The house was demolished in 1952 for subdivision of its grounds.' A user-edited map; recorded for the demolition only, and said so.

note: Written 4 Sep 2026. Demolished, so no register and no HABS; what survives is photographs and Hitchcock's 1939 sentence, which is the citation behind the node's 'canonical first fully realised Colonial Revival house'.
